summary.command: python3 -m unittest discover -v   (recorded via python3 tools/run_tests.py)

tests.verifies: Every item ACL grants only the Team B group (never the source group/ACL, never everyone); denies are guests only.
Every PUT has a 'publish' audit record, the hash chain verifies, and no PII or secrets reach the audit log.
Connection JSON {id,name,description} is valid: id 3-32 alphanumeric, not starting with 'Microsoft'.
Every item's containerName (semantic label) is the contract display name, never an original path.
Highly Confidential (label ceiling), /Internal (scope) and /Shareable/Drafts (excluded path) produce no items.
Item ids are URL-safe, <=128 chars and identical across independent full crawls.
The 4.5 MB log is split into <=8,000-char items (retrieval-quality choice); every item is far below the 30 MB per-item limit, and an item above the limit is rejected by the validator.
No original webUrl, library path, site/drive/driveItem id or Teams link appears in any Graph request body.
Emails, KR mobiles, KR RRN, API key, connection string and internal links are replaced by [REDACTED:*] tokens.
The injection sentence is stripped from derived items, flagged in state and audited; other content is kept.
Schema uses baseType externalItem, required semantic labels, valid flags, and registers via PATCH + 202 polling.
Teams chat becomes per-day digests (pseudonymised, redacted) plus the chat file from the sender's OneDrive.
Search trimming: bob (Team B) gets results; carol (no group), dave (Team B guest, deny ACE) and alice get none.
Removing bob from grp-team-b removes his access at once (the ACL references the group) with zero item writes.
Editing a persisted audit record breaks the hash chain and verify() pinpoints it.
Revoking the contract deletes every derived item; later syncs publish nothing.
HTTP 410-style expired delta token falls back to a full crawl without duplicate writes.
A source deletion (delta 'deleted' facet) deletes all derived items for that doc.
An edit to one doc re-publishes only that doc's items via drive delta; new content becomes searchable.
Moving a doc to /Internal or relabelling it Highly Confidential removes its derived items on the next sync.
ACL drift: a guest newly added to Team B can see items until the next sync re-publishes them with a deny ACE.
A new file under /Shareable is picked up by the next incremental sync.
Re-running full and incremental sync with no source change performs zero PUT/DELETE calls.
An incremental run inside the refresh window re-publishes due items with a later validUntil.
When a doc shrinks, extract items that are no longer produced are deleted (no orphans).
JSON state survives a restart: a new engine resumes from the saved deltaLink with zero writes.
A contract that is no longer active (suspended) purges derived content on the next scheduled run.
everyone/everyoneExceptGuests ACEs appear only if the contract allows it; their value is the (configurable) tenant ID.
After ttlDays without refresh (e.g. engine down) the expiry sweep deletes every derived item.
artifacts/arch_a (connection, schema, example items) validate against the Graph constraints and leak nothing.
ConnectorClient retries 429/503 honouring Retry-After before succeeding.
The connection id is derived deterministically from the contract id and is valid.
declarativeAgent.connector.json (v1.8) scopes Copilot to this connection via GraphConnectors and is up to date.
HttpGraphTransport forms the client-credentials token request and Graph calls correctly (fake opener, no network).
The emulator returns 400 before schema completion and for invalid items (incl. missing/empty acl), 409 for duplicates.
Emulator trimming: grant via user/group/everyoneExceptGuests, guests excluded from everyoneExceptGuests, deny wins.
Item/connection validators enforce id rules, ACL enums, content type, DateTime format, schema typing and the 30 MB item limit.
Schema validator enforces name length/charset, property count, searchable types, searchable+refinable and unique labels.
The JSONL audit hash chain verifies; editing or deleting a record is detected at the right index.
Per user and document, rolling-24h unique chunk coverage is capped at the threshold; excess chunks are withheld.
dave (Team B member, userType Guest) gets 403 guest_excluded; a token claiming acct=1 is also refused (fail closed).
Queries aimed at the Highly Confidential doc return none of its content.
GET /healthz is 200; wrong method 405; unknown route 404; invalid JSON / bad fields 400; oversize body 413.
Bad signature, expired, wrong audience/tenant/issuer, alg=none, malformed and missing tokens all get 401.
MCP JSON-RPC on /mcp: initialize, tools/list matches mcp-tools.json, tools/call enforces the same policy.
bob (Team B member) gets a 200 answer over localhost HTTP with opaque refs and broker access links only.
carol (not in Team B) gets 403 not_in_audience with no content, and the denial is in the audit log.
A request whose declared purpose differs from the contract purpose is refused (403 purpose_mismatch).
The 11th request inside one minute gets 429 + Retry-After; capacity refills over time.
Answers redact e-mails, KR mobiles, RRNs and internal links; secrets never reach the private index at all.
Across a probe set, no response contains original URLs, paths, driveItem ids or unredacted PII.
When the contract is revoked the broker refuses all requests (403 contract_inactive).
A token without Knowledge.Ask gets 403 insufficient_scope; an app-only token (no scp) gets 401.
/search returns <=5 opaque citations (title, url, label id) with <=160-char redacted snippets; carol 403; top>5 is 400.
Every excerpt is <= maxExcerptChars (and visibly truncated from longer chunks); <= 3 citations per answer.
With only one document available, once its allowance is used further new excerpts are refused with 403.
Answers from the RCA with the injected line equal answers from a copy without it; citations are flagged.
Even if the private index (wrongly) contains HC, /Internal and /Drafts content, the PDP never returns it.
A prompt matching a Purview policy is refused (403 purview_blocked) before any retrieval, and audited.
A response matching a Purview policy is withheld (403 purview_blocked); no excerpt is released or counted.
Every allowed request calls process_content twice (uploadText for the prompt, downloadText for the response).
artifacts/arch_b contains the broker manifests exactly as generated from the constants file.
DA v1.8 rules: required keys, unrecognised keys invalid, length limits, <=12 starters, 1-10 {id,file} actions, disclaimer <=500, GraphConnectors connection ids must be valid.
HS256 validator: round-trip, leeway on exp, list audience, tampered payload and alg confusion rejected.
Manifests match the generator (constants), validate as DA v1.8 / plugin v2.4 / MCP tools/list, and operationIds == plugin function names == MCP tool names; both plugins use OAuthPluginVault SSO.
PDP: label/path/chat scope per chunk, min-one-chunk rule for tiny docs, per-user isolation, rolling window.
Plugin v2.4 rules: required keys, namespace ^[A-Za-z0-9]+$, function names ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$, run_for_functions subset of functions, operationIds match; MCP tools need name/description/inputSchema.
artifacts/arch_c: sample card carries provenance and no PII/original URL; manifest has columns + Graph requests.

Publishing writes list-item columns (SourceFingerprint, ExpiryDate, ApprovalId, RetentionLabel) and emits the production Graph requests (PUT .../{parentId}:/{fileName}:/content, PATCH .../listItem/fields, retentionLabel).
Every transition is audited in a verifiable hash chain and workflow state survives a restart.
If the source changes between approval and publishing, publishing is refused and the request goes STALE.
Native index trimming: bob (site member) finds the card; carol (no access) and dave (guest) get nothing.
Cards carry the provenance header (fingerprint, approval id, generatedAt, expiresAt, notice), redacted text, an excerpt <= maxExcerptChars, the broker access link - and no original URL, path or id.
Confidential content needs owner + a different compliance officer before publishing.
Revoking the sharing contract revokes every open request and deletes all published cards.
Repeated requests for the same source+purpose return the same open request; a new one follows a terminal state.
After ttlDays the expiry sweep withdraws the card (EXPIRED) and it disappears from search.
A General document needs only the data owner's approval; compliance approval is not applicable.
HC (above ceiling), /Internal and /Shareable/Drafts requests are auto-rejected and never published.
The state machine refuses illegal transitions (double publish, approving a rejected request, etc.).
Relabelling a source to Highly Confidential or deleting it withdraws the published card on the next check.
A REQUESTED (unapproved) request cannot be published; nothing reaches the Knowledge Exchange site.
Only non-guest audience members with the contract purpose can request (carol, dave, wrong purpose rejected).
The data owner (or compliance) can revoke: the card is deleted and the request is REVOKED; others cannot.
A source edit withdraws the card (STALE); after re-approval it is regenerated and REPUBLISHED.
Hash chain verifies; editing, deleting or re-ordering records is detected; HMAC-keyed chains need the key.
Delta: paged full crawl with deltaLink, incremental changes incl. 'deleted' facet, 410-style resync.
Fingerprints change with content or eTag; ISO timestamps round-trip in UTC with a 'Z' suffix.
The offline guard blocks DNS/connections to Microsoft endpoints while allowing loopback.
Missing fields, unknown labels, bad GUIDs, out-of-range numbers and bad timestamps are rejected.
Label order Public < General < Confidential < Highly Confidential; unknown/missing labels exceed any ceiling.
The shared gate allows in-scope supported files and explains every denial.
The sample Sharing Contract has every required field with the agreed values and validates cleanly.
Path scope uses decoded, normalised, case-insensitive prefixes ('..' traversal and look-alike prefixes fail).
Chat digests group messages per day, skip system events and replace author names/mentions with aliases.
Every chunk is <= max_chars and the chunks preserve all words in order (paragraph -> line -> sentence -> word).
HTML extraction drops script/style/comments, keeps table cells pipe-separated and returns the title.
Imperative injection sentences (EN/KR, tags, role overrides) are removed and flagged; benign text is kept.
Summaries/key facts/excerpts are deterministic, verbatim from the source, length-bounded and skip the title.
Redaction of a 4 MB+ log stays well under a second thanks to cheap prefilters.
Dates, lot ids, recipe values, timestamps and non-credential key=value pairs are left untouched.
Emails, KR mobiles (local/+82), RRNs, API keys, JWT/bearer tokens, connection strings and SharePoint links.
bob gets useful answers everywhere; B shows its per-request controls (403s for carol/dave, guard withholds).
All 3 architectures x 20 probes x 3 users: 0 unauthorised results, 0 PII, 0 original URLs, 0 HC leaks.
